global_rules.rule: If a user request violates any rule herein, you must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
Perform one validated operation at a time (atomic operations) unless using approved batch endpoints.
Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.
Do not ask for further information; if a request is ambiguous, return the list of ambiguities and required fields.
All create or update requests must validate that every mandatory field is present.
Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes – rely solely on verified API results.
Access rights are defined by roles (admin, manager, agent, reporter) and grant granular CRUD permissions as listed.
Mandatory inputs for incident creation are opened_by, caller_id, short_description, impact, and urgency.
Priority is automatically calculated from the Impact × Urgency matrix.
All new incidents are created with status = new.
assigned_to must be an active user with the Agent or Manager role and a member of the specified assignment_group.
Valid status transitions are: new → in_progress/on_hold/resolved; in_progress → on_hold/resolved; on_hold → in_progress (requires on_hold_reason); resolved → closed/in_progress.
An incident cannot transition to resolved without resolution_code and resolution_notes (max 2000 characters).
Incidents in resolved status automatically transition to closed after 72 hours.
All changes must originate from a Change Request record; new changes start with status = new.
Change types are enumerated as standard, normal, or emergency.
A Problem must be created when a recurring incident pattern or major incident is identified.
A Problem must link all affected incidents via the incident_to_problem related list.
If a workaround is found, update the workaround field, set status = fix_in_progress, and publish workaround_notes to linked incidents and relevant knowledge articles.
A Problem can close only after a permanent fix is implemented via a linked normal or emergency Change Request.
Only CIs with status = in_use or maintenance may be linked to active incidents; retired or disposed CIs must not be linked.
Every CI must have an owner_id recorded.
SLA timers must be paused (stage = paused) when an incident is on_hold for Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem.
If SLA exceeds its target (stage = breached), set the escalation flag on the incident to true and automatically notify the Manager.
Only knowledge articles with state = published are searchable by the Reporter role.
When an incident is created, perform a knowledge search and link matching articles as used_as = suggested.
Ensure any user assigned to a record is active (users.active = true).
Return 403 Forbidden for permission‑denied actions, 409 Conflict for state conflicts, and apply exponential back‑off on rate‑limit violations.

triage.name: Initial Triage
steps: Validate confirmed user role (must be Reporter, Agent, Manager, or Administrator).
Check that all mandatory incident fields (opened_by, caller_id, short_description, impact, urgency) are present; if any are missing, stop and report the missing field.
Calculate incident priority using the Impact × Urgency matrix.
Search published knowledge articles for relevance and link as suggested.
If any validation fails, halt further processing.

housekeeping.name: Operational Housekeeping
steps: Log every create, update, and state transition with timestamp and user_id.
Verify referential integrity before closing any record.
Archive incidents that have been in closed status for more than 90 days.
Retain audit logs for the minimum compliance period defined by governance.

escalation.name: SLA Breach Escalation
steps: When stage becomes breached, set escalation = true on the incident.
Automatically send notification to the Manager.
Manager must review and reassign or approve corrective action.
must_not: Do not automatically close an incident that has breached SLA.
Do not bypass Manager approval for emergency changes without proper CAB override.

definitions.Incident: A record of an unplanned interruption or reduction in quality of an IT service, managed through its full lifecycle from creation to closure.
definitions.Change Request: A formal proposal to modify, add, or remove a configuration item or service, categorized as standard, normal, or emergency.
definitions.Problem: The underlying cause of one or more incidents, tracked to identify workarounds and permanent fixes.
definitions.Configuration Item (CI): Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver an IT service, stored in the configuration_item table with status and owner information.
definitions.SLA: Service Level Agreement – a contract that defines the target response and resolution times based on incident priority, with pause and breach handling rules.
definitions.Knowledge Article: A documented piece of information stored in kb_knowledge; only articles with state = published are visible to reporters.
definitions.Reporter: End‑user role that can create and view their own incidents/requests and search public knowledge.
definitions.Agent: Front‑line support role with full CRUD rights on operational records.
definitions.Manager: Supervisory role with full CRUD on operational tables, ability to reassign, approve changes, and receive escalations.
definitions.Administrator: System‑wide role with unrestricted CRUD access across all tables.
